data.title: Responsible Energy Provides Update on ESTCP AFFF Destruction Demonstration
data.description:

().

On September 15, 2026, Tetra Tech, Inc. publicly disclosed that preliminary testing conducted in July 2026 demonstrated that Responsible Energy's FRG achieved greater than 99.9% destruction and removal efficiency ("DRE") of undiluted aqueous film-forming foam ("AFFF"). Formal ESTCP validation trials are being conducted from September 15 through September 17, 2026. The Company will provide further information when validated results are available.

Inclusion of FRG in ESTCP does not constitute endorsement of FRG or the Company by the United States government.

Responsible Energy Corporation is a Canadian clean technology company commercializing its patented Free Radical Gasification (FRG™) technology for the destruction of PFAS, AFFF and other hazardous liquid waste streams. data.title: What's Moving Markets Today? — WSJ
data.description:
By Shradha Dinesh

Major indexes edged lower as the yield on the 10-year Treasury note pushed past 5%.

Markets have had a lot to digest this week: a quarter-point interest-rate hike, fluctuating fuel prices and big tech's P(doom), aka the probability that AI results in a existentially catastrophic outcome, according to the Silicon Valley ecosystem.

Here's what is moving markets today:

Tech stocks: As bond yields climbed, driven by higher oil prices, tech stocks broadly flattened. Today's standouts are those behind AI infrastructure. Sandisk and Coherent posted 8% and 4% intraday gains, respectively.

Oil prices: Oil prices extended declines for a third consecutive session Friday on news that damage to Saudi Arabia's East-West pipeline and to an oil tanker hit in the Strait of Hormuz late on Thursday may not be as extensive as feared. Before prices reversed course, Brent crude recovered some of its losses after Bloomberg reported that Saudi Arabia told at least two European customers that they would not receive crude deliveries next month. Brent crude is just under $104 a barrel, or down 1%.

It's another big day for crypto and alternative assets: Bitcoin broke above $80,000. Strategy, Coinbase and MARA holdings are up more than 10%. Exchanges, like Robinhood and Bullish, and cryptocurrency miners are not far behind. The gains follow some new rules allowing exchanges to offer tokenized stocks and regulatory agencies stepping in to oversee crypto after the failure of a major bill this week.

This item is part of a Wall Street Journal live coverage event. The full stream can be found by searching P/WSJL (WSJ Live Coverage).

data.title: Volkswagen Warns on Profit After Big Porsche Write-Down — WSJ
data.description:
By Andrea Figueras and Mauro Orru

Volkswagen slashed its full-year profit forecast after flagging roughly $11.5 billion of impairment charges linked to its stake in Porsche, tough trading in China and its restructuring efforts.

The German carmaker said Friday that it now expected an operating return on sales of up to 1% this year, down from its prior estimate of between 4% and 5.5%. The new forecast, announced just before the market closed in Germany, sent Volkswagen shares down more than 5%.

The profit warning comes as Volkswagen contends with a range of challenges, including U.S. tariffs, rising manufacturing costs and increasingly fierce competition from Chinese automakers-in both China and Europe.

Earlier this month, Volkswagen's supervisory board approved a plan to double job cuts at the automaker to 100,000 and halve its model portfolio in a bid to remain competitive.

On Friday, the company said a further deterioration in market conditions-especially in China-as well as a shift in demand in favor of battery-electric vehicles would weigh on earnings, particularly at Audi and its Volkswagen brands.

Volkswagen said new assumptions about Porsche's prospects would result in a write-down of about 6 billion euros, the equivalent of about $6.89 billion. Volkswagen holds a stake of more than 75% in the sports-car brand.

Porsche has been contending with its own challenges, including a big bet on EVs that failed to pay off, U.S. tariffs and declining demand in China.

Volkswagen said it would take a further 2 billion euros in impairments in the second half of the year because of developments in the Chinese market and restructuring costs related to early-retirement programs and the planned sale of its Osnabrück factory in Germany.

The company said earlier this month that it was selling its Osnabrück plant to Israel's Aurelius Capital and the state of Lower Saxony, which aim to repurpose the site to make defense equipment.

In total, Volkswagen said, "special effects" amounting to 10 billion euros would weigh on operating profit this year, of which 900 million euros worth were already reported in the first half.

The company said revenue for the year is now expected to decline to about 315 billion euros from 321.9 billion euros in 2025, roughly in line with the midpoint of its previous guidance.

Volkswagen said its outlook was based on the assumption that tariffs would remain unchanged. It also noted that its estimates didn't take into account possible future effects from the war in the Middle East.

The company plans to publish its third-quarter report on Oct. 29.

Write to Andrea Figueras at andrea.figueras@wsj.com and Mauro Orru at mauro.orru@wsj.com

data.title: This Little-Known Chip Stock Has Doubled. Wall Street Is Getting Bullish. — Barrons.com
data.description:
By Ty Roush

MACOM Technology Solutions Holdings, a lesser-known semiconductor company benefiting from the accelerating data-center buildout, rose again Friday as Wall Street takes notice.

Shares of MACOM rose 4.7% and have surged 117% over the last year. The broader iShares Semiconductor ETF added 1%, while Broadcom advanced 2.2% and NXP Semiconductors N.V. fell 0.9%.

BMO Capital Markets upgraded MACOM to Outperform from Market Perform Thursday, even as its shares remain 33% below their all-time closing high of $409.68.

BMO is "excited" about MACOM's profit growth being driven by strong demand from artificial-intelligence data centers, while defense market "remains resilient," and that space is set to become a "material contributor" to growth in 2027, analyst Harsh Kumar wrote.

Kumar reiterated BMO's $335 price target for MACOM shares.

Wall Street has issued largely bullish views on MACOM shares in recent weeks, with 12 of the 16 firms polled by FactSet rating the stock a Buy.

Among them, Jefferies issued a price target of $450 for MACOM stock, about 71% above its Thursday closing price of $263.14, following the company's latest earnings in August.

Quarterly revenue rose 36% to $342.2 million-exceeding Wall Street estimates of $336 million, according to FactSet-as net income surged 176% to $100.7 million, MACOM reported last month.

MACOM announced a new suite of microchips Thursday designed to make optical communication inside AI data centers twice as fast as its earlier products. CEO Stephen Daly said the new chips would help deliver peak performance while cutting down on development efforts.

The announcement helped lift MACOM shares 4.5% Thursday, following a 4.8% increase on Wednesday.

data.title: Bitcoin Trades Above $80,000 to Clock Third Day of Gains — 2nd Update
data.description:
By Joseph Wilkins and Kirk Maltais

Bitcoin rose for a third consecutive day, topping the $80,000 level that has been a stubborn cap in recent weeks.

The move higher comes after Thursday's session saw a tech-fueled relief rally with broad gains seen from chip makers to data-storage companies across the major indexes. This uptick is being seen in both major cryptocurrencies and in stocks for companies involved with blockchain technology.

The flagship cryptocurrency rose 5.9% at $80,966, solidifying a course for a positive end to the week after it had slipped to a near four-week low on the U.S. Senate's rejection of the Clarity Act on Tuesday.

Gains were not limited to major cryptocurrencies, with Coinbase Global climbing 11%, Strategy Inc. rising 13% and Circle Internet Group up 7%.

The Federal Reserve's quarter-point interest-rate hike Wednesday has complicated the path for nonyielding assets such as bitcoin and gold, which tend to lose their relative shine in a rate-raising cycle when compared with the return offered by bonds.

The rate hike is one reason fund traders posted net outflows for bitcoin exchange-traded funds for six out of seven prior trading sessions. Flows changed course Thursday, posting a net inflow of $159.5 million into those ETFs on Thursday, according to data from CoinGlass.

Bitcoin could outperform gold in the coming months if investors unwind some of the short positions surrounding cryptocurrency ETFs, according to JPMorgan.

Analysts led by JPMorgan's Nikolaos Panigirtzoglou wrote that short interest in the flagship bitcoin ETF--iShares Bitcoin Trust ETF, or IBIT--remains close to year-to-date highs, while short interest in gold ETFs stands below historical averages.

"This contrast suggests that bitcoin still faces an overall more skeptical positioning backdrop than gold, perhaps due to more elevated hedging demand, despite the recent inflows and build up of futures positioning," the analysts wrote.

Analysts are eyeing targets above the $80,000 mark should bitcoin continue its upward momentum. In a note published Friday, analysts with Coinbase Research said resistance targets above $80,0000 are $83,000, then $90,000, and then $95,000.

Should the rally lose steam and see bitcoin retreating back below $70,000, prices are expected to keep falling back to yearly lows around $58,000, said Coinbase in its note.

data.title: Tesla Q3 Deliveries Could Beat Expectations, Says Barclays — Analyst Calls Fundamentals An ‘Afterthought’ To AI Story
data.description:
Key points:
  • Barclays said Tesla’s ramp-up of FSD supports its autonomous-driving ambitions and could help improve margins.
  • The firm maintained an ‘Equal Weight’ rating and $370 price target.
  • Goldman Sachs cut its Q3 delivery estimate to 435,000 vehicles from 490,000 units.

Tesla (TSLA) was in the spotlight on Friday after Barclays said the EV maker could deliver more vehicles than expected in the third quarter and added that its autonomous driving technologies could boost margins.

At the time of writing, TSLA shares were trading 1% lower, heading for their first weekly fall in three weeks.

Barclays Sees Autonomous Driving Boost

Barclays analyst Dan Levy expects Tesla to deliver 475,000 vehicles in the third quarter (Q3), above the 466,000 estimate reportedly compiled by Bloomberg. This also beats Goldman Sachs’ estimates from earlier this week.

The firm maintained an ‘Equal Weight’ rating and $370 price target, according to The Fly. It represents a 2.2% upside from current levels.

Barclays said Tesla’s ramp-up of Full Self-Driving (FSD) supports the company’s broader autonomous-driving ambitions and could help improve margins. However, Levy said Tesla’s underlying fundamentals remain “mostly an afterthought” to its AI efforts.

FSD Could Find Favor In Europe, But Cybercab Faces Domestic Scrutiny

Tesla has increasingly positioned AI and autonomy at the center of its long-term growth story, spanning FSD, its Robotaxi network, and Optimus humanoid robots.

Tesla has continued to update its Full Self-Driving software, recently rolling out FSD v14.3.9. The carmaker is also pushing to expand FSD internationally, with Slovenia becoming the sixth European country to approve the system ahead of a potential broader EU rollout.

However, FSD still requires active driver supervision and does not make Tesla vehicles fully autonomous.

Meanwhile, its Cybercab is facing fresh regulatory scrutiny. The National Highway Traffic Safety Administration (NHTSA) has reportedly asked Tesla to explain by September 30 how it certified the robotaxi, including whether temporary human-operated controls were used during the process.

Goldman Sachs Has A More Cautious View

Barclays’ delivery forecast contrasts sharply with Goldman Sachs, which cut its Q3 estimate to 435,000 vehicles from 490,000.

Goldman said sales in Tesla’s key U.S., Chinese and European markets were tracking below its earlier expectations, even if strength in Southeast Asia, South America and Australia could partly offset that weakness.

Tesla delivered 480,126 vehicles in the second quarter (Q2), rebounding sharply from 358,023 in Q1. Barclays’ estimate would represent only a slight sequential decline, while Goldman’s forecast implies a drop of about 9%.

Retail’s Take On TSLA

Retail sentiment for TSLA on Stocktwits remained ‘extremely bearish’ over the past 24 hours.

TSLA is down more than 17% so far in 2026, easily the worst-performing stock among the so-called Magnificent 7.

data.title: Expectation vs reality: Why you should not assume 20%+ equity returns-what Nifty 500 historical data reveals
data.description:
New Delhi, Sept. 18 -- When equity markets deliver strong returns, it can be easy for investors to start treating those gains as a new baseline. But history suggests that very high returns are not what investors experience most often.

In an X post, Niranjan Avasthi, President at Edelweiss Asset Management, highlighted the importance of keeping return expectations realistic. "When markets deliver unusually strong returns, it is tempting to treat those outcomes as the new normal," he noted.

Data reveals that across 258 three-year rolling return observations for the Nifty 500 TRI since 2005, the most common outcome was a CAGR of 10%-20%. This range accounted for 119 observations, or 46% of the total.

A three-year rolling return measures the annualised return earned over every possible three-year period within the data set, with the observation moving forward month by month.

For example, one observation would measure the annualised return from January 2005 to January 2008, the next from February 2005 to February 2008, and so on. This gives investors a much broader picture of the range of outcomes than simply looking at the Nifty 500's return over one fixed three-year period.

The data shows that a three-year CAGR between 10% and 20% was the most frequently observed outcome.

"Across 258 monthly observations of rolling 3-year CAGR returns since 2005 for the Nifty 500, the most common outcome was a return between 10% and 20%. This range occurred 119 times, i.e., 46% of all observations, making it the clearest centre of gravity in the data," Avasthi mentioned.

"The latest rolling three-year CAGR is 12.9%, broadly within this dominant band. This does not indicate weak performance; rather, it is consistent with the return experience investors have encountered most frequently," he added.

This does not mean investors will earn 10%-20% in every three-year period. Equity returns can vary sharply depending on when an investor enters and exits the market.

The data shows that strong three-year outcomes were relatively less frequent. "Higher-return periods do occur, but they should be viewed as a bonus rather than the baseline," he noted.

He added, "Returns between 20% and 30% appeared in 32 observations, or 12% of the sample. Returns above 30% occurred 41 times, representing 16%. These phases can materially accelerate wealth creation, but their relative rarity makes them unsuitable as permanent assumptions for financial plans or investor expectations."

At the other end, 13 observations, or 5%, recorded returns between -10% and 0%. Another 53 observations, or 21%, delivered returns between 0% and 10%. No three-year rolling period in the dataset recorded a CAGR below -10%.

Not necessarily.

"The historical average is 17.5%, while the median is 15.0%, reinforcing that mid-teen expectations are a more practical planning anchor than exceptional bull-market outcomes," he noted.

According to Avasthi, this suggests that investors may find mid-teen return expectations more practical for financial planning than assuming that exceptionally strong market returns will continue.

He summed up the point: "Equity investing rewards patience, but expectations matter. Investors who plan around sustainable mid-teen outcomes are less likely to be disappointed by normal market cycles or tempted to chase risk after unusually strong periods."

"Mid-teen returns are the planning anchor; exceptional returns are like bonus," he noted.

data.title: Micron Faces Growing China Threat. It's a Bigger Problem for Memory-Chip Rivals. — Barrons.com
data.description:
By Adam Clark

Chinese memory companies aren't slowing down. China's CXMT is reportedly planning on expanding its portfolio into flash memory, which could intensify competition for Micron Technology and SK Hynix.

CXMT-which is a specialist in dynamic random-access memory (DRAM)- intends to establish a NAND flash memory research-and-development production line at a new factory in Beijing, Reuters reported Friday, citing people familiar with the matter. CXMT didn't immediately respond to a request for comment.

DRAM is short-term working memory that computers and AI hardware use to manage active data and running processes. NAND flash memory is used for longer-term storage.

CXMT's move threatens to make the NAND market look pretty crowded. Chinese company Yangtze Memory Technologies, or YMTC, is already making its presence felt in the flash-memory sector, taking 14% of the market in the second quarter of the year, according to Counterpoint Research.

If CXMT makes a serious push into flash memory the NAND market could be further fragmented. Currently the biggest player is South Korea's Samsung Electronics with a 28% share, followed by its domestic peer SK Hynix with a 19% share. Among U.S. companies, Micron had roughly 15% share in the second quarter, while Sandisk had 11%, Counterpoint data showed.

As for what it means for shareholders, both Micron and SK Hynix currently generate about a quarter of their revenue from NAND. However, Micron has less of the market to lose to Chinese companies than its Korean peer.

In the short-term, both Micron and SK Hynix investors can be reassured that the memory-chip market is growing so fast that there is still massive revenue and profit growth to go around. The DRAM market grew 57% in the second quarter from the prior quarter and NAND grew 70%, Counterpoint said.

Additionally, there's no confirmation when or if CXMT intends to move into commercial production of NAND chips. If it does, then it is likely that CXMT would concentrate first on the domestic Chinese market. That could mean it is a bigger threat to its domestic rival YMTC than Micron or SK Hynix.

Micron shares were up 1.1% in early trading and American depositary receipts of SK Hynix rose 1.2%.

data.title: Why France's budget problems have driven its bond risk premium to 2012 highs
data.description:
By Yoruk Bahceli and Leigh Thomas

The premium France pays to borrow on the bond markets compared to Germany rose to more than a whole percentage point on Friday for the first time since the euro zone debt crisis, underscoring investor unease with its stretched finances ahead of elections next year.

Here's a look at what's at stake:

1/ WHY HAS THE PREMIUM INVESTORS DEMAND TO HOLD FRENCH BONDS RISEN OVER 100 BASIS POINTS?

France's 10-year borrowing costs have risen much faster than any other developed economy's in a global bond selloff driven by rising energy prices in recent weeks. Investors, worried about long-term finances across developed economies, are growing concerned as France struggles to cut its high budget deficit ahead of a presidential election next year that could make that task even harder.

The French government must now pay a 104-basis-point premium on its 10-year bonds over Germany's for the first time since 2012 as investors seek more compensation to hold its debt.

This is just the latest milestone for the spread between the two yields, which has doubled since a snap election in 2024 delivered a fractured parliament that has made it much harder to cut France's budget deficit, one of the highest in the euro zone.

The government is trying to reduce it from 5.4% of output this year to 5% next year through €54 billion of tough spending cuts. Opposition parties are likely to challenge them in the coming months, potentially bringing the government down.

France will miss this year's original 5% target due to lower-than-expected growth. Rising energy prices due to the Middle East conflict, which have prompted investors to bet on further European Central Bank rate hikes, could hurt growth even further.

Concern is also mounting that next year's presidential election could derail efforts to lower the deficit as the far-right's Marine Le Pen and the far-left's Jean-Luc Melenchon are the frontrunners.

Melenchon's call on the French central bank to cancel the government debt it holds has rattled investors, while Le Pen, who is leading the polls, is advocating lowering the retirement age for some people, which would add to the pressure on the country's finances.

Italy's bond spread has also risen, but much less than the 40 basis points rise in France since June.

2/ WHAT DOES IT MEAN FOR GOVERNMENT FINANCES?

It makes new borrowing more expensive and adds to rising debt-servicing costs. These have already become France's biggest budget expense, as it refinances hundreds of billions of COVID-era debt borrowed at ultra-low rates.

The government already expects debt-servicing costs will be €4.5 billion more than expected this year because of higher interest rates and a further €10 billion higher next year.

Economists worry that with growth low and interest rates rising, France faces a snowball effect where borrowing costs spiral higher unless the government manages to post a primary surplus, which it is far from doing.

3/ WHY DOES IT MATTER FOR MARKETS?

It's a particularly telling sign that France's bond market, the euro zone's largest and traditionally regarded as a relatively safe asset, is losing that status.

After all, the last time France paid a three-digit premium over Germany was at the height of the euro zone debt crisis in 2012, when the future of the euro was in question.

France is also paying a higher premium than Italy, a country that has higher debt and much lower credit ratings.

Many investors say they are reluctant to favour French bonds in their portfolios.

Paying a 100 basis-point spread over Germany shows "France has real problems, and that they're not going to be solved anytime soon," said David Zahn, head of European fixed income at Franklin Templeton.

4/ COULD THE SPREAD RISE EVEN FURTHER?

Given the scale of the move already, some analysts see limited scope for a significant move higher in the near term.

"At some point, unless you think they're on a road to something really horrible, you've got to make the judgement that there's enough compensation for taking on the sovereign risk," said L&G's head of macro strategy Chris Jeffery, who recently closed a position betting against French bonds.

But further political uncertainty could still push the spread wider, analysts say, for example if the government falls and leaves France without a budget, or Melenchon and Le Pen face each other in the second round of the presidential election. Societe Generale has not ruled out a move to 120 basis points.

data.title: Bitcoin Trades Above $80,000 to Clock Third Day of Gains — Update
data.description:
By Joseph Wilkins and Kirk Maltais

Bitcoin rose for a third consecutive day, topping the $80,000 level that has been a stubborn cap in recent weeks.

The move higher comes after Thursday's session saw a tech-fueled relief rally with broad gains seen from chip makers to data-storage companies across the major indexes. This uptick is being seen in both major cryptocurrencies and in stocks for companies involved with blockchain technology.

The flagship cryptocurrency rose 5.9% at $80,966, solidifying a course for a positive end to the week after it had slipped to a near four-week low on the U.S. Senate's rejection of the Clarity Act on Tuesday.

Gains were not limited to major cryptocurrencies, with Coinbase Global climbing 11%, Strategy Inc. rising 13% and Circle Internet Group up 7%.

The Federal Reserve's quarter-point interest-rate hike Wednesday has complicated the path for nonyielding assets such as bitcoin and gold, which tend to lose their relative shine in a rate-raising cycle when compared with the return offered by bonds.

The rate hike is one reason fund traders posted net outflows for bitcoin exchange-traded funds for six out of seven prior trading sessions. Flows changed course Thursday, posting a net inflow of $159.5 million into those ETFs on Thursday, according to data from CoinGlass.

Bitcoin could outperform gold in the coming months if investors unwind some of the short positions surrounding cryptocurrency ETFs, according to JPMorgan.

Analysts led by JPMorgan's Nikolaos Panigirtzoglou wrote that short interest in the flagship bitcoin ETF--iShares Bitcoin Trust ETF, or IBIT--remains close to year-to-date highs, while short interest in gold ETFs stands below historical averages.

"This contrast suggests that bitcoin still faces an overall more skeptical positioning backdrop than gold, perhaps due to more elevated hedging demand, despite the recent inflows and build up of futures positioning," the analysts wrote.

Analysts are eyeing targets above the $80,000 mark should bitcoin continue its upward momentum. In a note published Friday, analysts with Coinbase Research said resistance targets above $80,0000 are $83,000, then $90,000, and then $95,000.

Should the rally lose steam and see bitcoin retreating back below $70,000, prices are expected to keep falling back to yearly lows around $58,000, said Coinbase in its note.

data.title: Xenon downgraded at Deutsche Bank after pause in depression trials
data.description:
Xenon Pharmaceuticals fell 30% to reach its lowest level since November after the company paused enrollment in Phase 3 depression trials for its lead asset, azetukalner, following safety concerns, leading to a downgrade at Deutsche Bank.

Analyst David Hoang downgraded the Canadian biotech to Hold from Buy after the company paused enrollments in multiple late-stage trials for azetukalner in major depressive disorder and bipolar depression in reaction to several neuropsychiatric adverse events, including psychosis.

However, Xenon management argued that the decision was a temporary measure taken as a precaution and there won’t be an impact on ongoing epilepsy studies.The nature of the events, as well as their severity and frequency, were in line with the known safety and tolerability profile of the drug, the company added.

Despite those remarks, Hoang said, “We disagree and believe this impairs the molecule’s overall profile as a potential best-in-class drug that would become the go-to, branded antiseizure medication of choice in focal epilepsy.” The analyst slashed his price target on XENE to $46 from $90 per share.

However, Stifel, Baird, and RBC Capital Markets were among the firms to reaffirm their bullish ratings on the stock. While the surprising decision leads to uncertainty, "we're confident there’s minimal readthrough to FOS," Stifel analyst Paul Matteis wrote with a Buy rating, according to Bloomberg.

RBC Capital Markets analyst Brian Abrahams reiterated his Outperform rating yet trimmed his price target to $70 from $81, noting, “We believe the core value remains epilepsy and do not see any major risk to the filing timelines or commercial launch.”

Baird analyst Brian Skorney also sounded cautious, lowering his price target to $90 from $97 despite an outperforming rating. “We still think the MDD study is adequately powered into the 1Q topline, and we see low-rate psychosis as an AE neurologists are equipped to manage,” Skorney added.

data.title: Tesla Slips 1% as $16.8 Billion AI Fab Meets a Naming Fight
data.description:
Tesla , the electric-vehicle and robotics company, added a trademark fight to the already ambitious execution story surrounding its planned $16.8 billion Terafab chip complex. Shares slipped roughly 1% to $362.84 Friday. The valuation picture adds another layer: the stock sits 8.66% above its $333.92 GF Value, suggesting investors are still paying a premium for Tesla's long-term growth ambitions.

Tesla and SpaceX are seeking a federal ruling that the Terafab name does not infringe TERA-print's trademark rights. The planned Texas operation would manufacture, package and test advanced logic and memory chips for Optimus robots, Cybercabs and SpaceX data centers, while Tesla filed three Terafab-related trademark applications in May. The legal dispute may grab headlines, but the much bigger question is whether Tesla can turn a huge capital commitment into reliable semiconductor output.

That is where the investment case gets tougher. Bringing more chip production in-house could give Tesla and SpaceX greater control over supply, technology road maps and potentially costs. But control comes with execution risk: yields, utilization, engineering talent and manufacturing discipline all become their problem. A trademark victory would clear one obstacle. It would not prove the economics. Investors ultimately need Terafab to produce competitive chips at scale and earn sensible returns on that $16.8 billion commitment.

data.title: SpaceX Lands 3 Additional NASA Crew Missions Under $946M Contract Modification
data.description:
Key points:
  • NASA said the arrangement helps maintain two commercial crew partners for continued access to the ISS.
  • The agreement includes ground, launch, in-orbit and recovery services, plus cargo transport and lifeboat capability.
  • Crew-12 remains docked at the station, marking SpaceX’s 12th crew rotation mission for NASA.

NASA on Friday awarded SpaceX (SPCX) three additional missions to continue regular crew transportation to the International Space Station through a modification to its Commercial Crew Transportation Capability (CCtCap) contract.

The award covers the Crew-15, Crew-16 and Crew-17 missions and brings SpaceX’s total missions under the contract to 17.

$946M Contract Covers Three Missions

The firm-fixed-price, indefinite-delivery/indefinite-quantity contract modification is valued at $946 million for all three missions and related mission services. The amount covers ground, launch, in-orbit, return and recovery operations, as well as cargo transportation for each mission and a lifeboat capability while docked to the International Space Station.

The period of performance runs through 2030, bringing the total value of SpaceX’s CCtCap contract with NASA to $5.92 billion.

Award Follows May Notice Of Intent

The award follows NASA’s May notice of intent to purchase the three additional missions. NASA said the current sole-source modification does not prevent the agency from seeking additional contract modifications for transportation services in the future, as needed.

NASA originally awarded CCtCap contracts to Boeing (BA) and SpaceX (SPCX) in 2014 through a public-private partnership under its Commercial Crew Program.

Under CCtCap, NASA certifies that a provider’s space transportation system meets agency requirements before the system flies missions with astronauts.

NASA certified SpaceX for crew transportation in November 2020. The company’s Crew-12 mission is currently in orbit and docked to the International Space Station. SpaceX uses its Dragon spacecraft and Falcon 9 rocket for NASA crew missions, transporting up to four astronauts along with critical cargo to the station.

NASA’s Commercial Crew Program uses commercial spacecraft and launch systems to provide human transportation to and from the International Space Station through partnerships with U.S. private industry. The program currently includes both SpaceX and Boeing as commercial crew providers.

Retail View On SPCX

Retail sentiment on Stocktwits for SPCX remained in “bullish” territory over the past 24 hours, while message volume was “low.”

SpaceX shares are currently trading at around $152, above its IPO price of $135 but below its all-time high of about $225.

data.title: With Oil Hovering at $100 a Barrel, Recycled Plastic is the Affordability Solution Hiding in Plain Sight
data.description:
NEW YORK CITY, NY / ACCESS Newswire / September 18, 2026 / The material once dismissed as too expensive, too messy, and too difficult to scale has become one of the most practical tools for keeping modern life affordable. The Age of Parity has made it viable; SMX is making it real.

Recycled plastic, long treated as the greener but costlier alternative to virgin plastic, is being redefined by war, oil volatility, supply-chain pressure, tariffs, regulation, and new verification technology. What was once framed mostly as an environmental choice is now becoming something far more urgent: an economic solution.

That is the new reality behind the "Age of Parity" - the moment when recycled plastic and virgin plastic begin converging in cost, and when certified recycling becomes not just good for the planet, but essential to preserving the price structure of modern life.

Plastic is not a side issue in the global economy. It is the material foundation of everyday affordability. It protects food, preserves medicine, ships goods, supports electronics, enables cars, powers packaging, reduces weight, lowers transportation costs, and helps make countless consumer products cheaper and more accessible.

For decades, that system depended on one basic assumption: virgin plastic would remain cheap, abundant, and predictable.

That assumption is now breaking.

The war in Iran, instability across oil and petrochemical markets, and pressure on global supply chains are exposing how vulnerable the plastic economy has become. Virgin plastic is structurally tied to oil and gas. When energy markets spike, virgin plastic reprices with them. Feedstock, processing, shipping, and supply-chain risk all move together.

Recycled plastic is different.

Its costs are driven more by collection, sorting, cleaning, processing, logistics, and certification. Those costs have historically made recycled plastic more expensive than virgin material. But as virgin plastic becomes more volatile and expensive, and as verification technology reduces the uncertainty around recycled content, the old economics are changing.

That is why recycled plastic may be emerging as the unexpected affordability tool of the next decade.

For years, recycled plastic carried what many called a "green premium." But that premium was never simply about the plastic itself. It was also about distrust. Buyers could not always prove where recycled material came from, what it contained, whether it met specification, or whether its chain of custody was reliable. That uncertainty became a hidden tax on recycling.

SMX's technology is designed to remove that tax.

Through its molecular marking and digital traceability platform, SMX gives physical materials a persistent, verifiable identity. Its technology can embed an invisible molecular marker into plastic and other materials, then link that marker to secure digital records that travel with the material across its lifecycle. That record can verify origin, composition, recycled content, authenticity, chain of custody, lifecycle history, and reuse potential.

In simpler terms, SMX helps plastic prove what it is.

That proof matters because the next stage of recycling will not be built on promises. It will be built on certification. Manufacturers, regulators, brands, and consumers increasingly need to know whether recycled material is real, where it came from, how it moved, what it contains, and whether it can be trusted at industrial scale.

SMX's core capabilities include molecular marking, instant authentication, blockchain-backed digital records, digital material passports, provenance tracking, chain-of-custody verification, recycled-content certification, lifecycle monitoring, audit-ready compliance, and data-backed recycling validation. Together, these tools help turn recycled plastic from an uncertain input into a trusted industrial material.

That distinction could have direct economic consequences.

If certified recycled plastic can be authenticated, trusted, and scaled, manufacturers gain another reliable input stream at a time when virgin material is becoming more expensive and less predictable. That can help reduce pressure on the cost of everyday goods - food packaging, cleaning products, electronics, apparel, medical supplies, building materials, and consumer products.

This is where recycling stops being a climate slogan and becomes economic infrastructure.

The world already produces enormous amounts of plastic waste, much of it mismanaged or lost from the productive economy. In a world of rising material costs, that waste is no longer just an environmental failure. It is stranded value. Recovering it, identifying it, certifying it, and returning it to manufacturing could become one of the clearest ways to protect affordability without sacrificing performance or compliance.

That is the deeper meaning of the Age of Parity.

It is not simply about recycled plastic catching up to virgin plastic on price. It is about the global materials economy recognizing that certainty has value. Proof has value. Traceability has value. A plastic supply chain less exposed to oil shocks has value.

The war in Iran has accelerated the lesson. When oil and petrochemical markets are disrupted, the shock does not stay in energy. It moves into packaging, retail, transportation, medicine, food, and household budgets. Plastic price volatility becomes consumer price volatility.

The answer is not simply to use less plastic. Modern life depends on plastic too deeply for that to be realistic. The answer is to make plastic smarter, more traceable, more recoverable, and more reusable.

That is what SMX is positioning itself to enable.

By connecting physical materials to secure digital proof, SMX helps create the infrastructure for a new materials economy - one where plastic is not anonymous, recycling is not guesswork, and sustainability claims are not accepted on faith.

The Age of Parity signals a turning point. Plastic is being repriced. Recycling is being revalued. Proof is becoming infrastructure. And the material once seen as the expensive alternative may become one of the most practical ways to keep modern life affordable.

ABOUT SMX (SECURITY MATTERS) PLC

SMX (Security Matters) PLC develops molecular traceability and material authentication technologies designed to strengthen supply-chain transparency and integrity across global industries. Its platform embeds invisible molecular markers directly into physical materials-including solids, liquids, and gases-allowing them to carry a persistent identity that can be detected and verified throughout their lifecycle.
